restrictions: Applies to the selected target poseidon-orchard-r1-prefix-v1 only (one partial round plus the eight fixed full rounds); the construction relies on the first two full rounds being skippable on a line and gives no claim for other round counts.

The run is probabilistic: at most two independent centres on two different lines; the claimed success probability is for the whole run, with the implemented halts of proof.md section 4 counted as failures.

heuristics.statement: For a centre c uniform in [0, 2^254) and line j in {0,1,2}, the number K of nonzero squares among the F_p-roots of the monic odd-part polynomial g_c (degree 39062) is Poisson with mean 1/2, independent across centres and lines, so one centre succeeds with probability 1 - exp(-1/2) = 0.3935 and two centres with probability 0.632 (claimed: 0.60, which needs a per-centre probability of only 0.37).
heuristics.scope: Odd-part polynomials of the Orchard r = 1 digest along the three lines of proof.md section 2 over the Pallas base field; the program of proof.md section 4 with at most two centres; algorithmic random words modelled as independent uniform.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 65 complete single-centre executions at the selected target (28 successes) and from earlier toy analogues over a 38-bit prime (degrees 125 to 15625, up to 600,000 centres, rate 0.3937 +- 0.001) to the full field; the target-size sample cannot separate 0.3935 from nearby rates at its width and is used only to support the weaker per-centre bound 0.37.
heuristics.limitations: No proof that g_c behaves like a random polynomial for the root count; the toy rates and the target-size rate are measurements, not a bound; the certificates show only that found roots yield collisions and say nothing about their frequency; the random words of the program come from a deterministic generator.

heuristics.statement: The counts of proof.md sections 6 and 7 are the totals of an instrumented execution of the described program under the stated rules: 1 per field operation, 1 per element load or store, 4 control operations per 16 elements of a straight loop (12 per 16-element transform block), 237 per reduced permutation evaluation of stage B, and 16-element register blocks as the only register assumption.
heuristics.scope: All stages of the program of proof.md section 4 at the target dimensions (m = 39062, N = 98304, N' = 49152, H = 49152).
heuristics.extrapolation: None beyond the executed dimensions; the worst case for two centres is formed from the measured data-independent stages and the implemented budgets of the data-dependent stages.
heuristics.limitations: The instrumented source is not shipped (candidate files are restricted to declared Python experiments), so the totals cannot be recomputed from the package; word-level costs outside the stated rules (cache, address arithmetic beyond the control charges) are not part of the model.

heuristics.statement: The half-gcd stage on (g, R - 1) stays within 800,000,000 charged operations; the stage has this budget as an implemented halt and a halt counts as a failure of the run.
heuristics.scope: Stage D of proof.md section 4 for inputs produced by stages B and C.
heuristics.extrapolation: From 65 executions (stage totals 790,284,664 to 790,285,374) to all inputs; exceeding the budget requires a non-normal remainder sequence (probability about 1/p per step) or a gcd of large degree.
heuristics.limitations: Cost concentration is observed and argued, not proved; the budget itself bounds the loss.
